_comment_: P4-A: per-seat capacity map. Replaces the legacy single '4 Devin workers' cap with per-provider + per-model caps, a RAM governor, and a metered-seat class so prepaid-quota seats are exhausted before paid-per-token ones.
_comment_order: Selection order (fleet-ops#387): free lanes first, then prepaid-quota alternating (never stack), then metered last. prepaid_providers_in_order is expiry-first among prepaid (devin -> cursor -> cline -> ollama). Implemented in seat-lib.sh pick_seat; this file is data only. Classes are free / prepaid-quota / metered. subscription is accepted as an alias of prepaid-quota.
_comment_ram_governor: ram_gb_per_worker=0.6 (2026-08-27 ~20:50 IST, Nish packet 'right-size the RAM governor', re-measured by agent). PREVIOUS: 1.5 (fleet-ops#489/PR#590, 2026-08-26) which deliberately kept lanes tight (~4-5) using the formula min(memory.current p95 * 3, 1.5). #489 settled the METRIC (cgroup memory.current, not process VmRSS — VmRSS undercounts ~100x) and that metric stands. This change lowers the CLAMP, not the metric. BACKSTOPS (unchanged, proven): per-worker MemoryHigh=3G/MemoryMax=6G (throttle then hard kill), system-scope user-1000.slice MemoryHigh=12G (fleet-ops#71, drilled 2026-08-26), systemd-oomd kill at 80%/60s. These bound the tail — the p95*3 governor clamp was more conservative than they require. FRESH MEASUREMENT (2026-08-27 ~20:50 IST, 5 live pi --print workers): MemAvailable 11.3G, /proc/pressure/memory some avg10=0.0%, worker cgroup MemoryCurrent non-throttled max 0.86G median ~0.17G (one throttled at 2.93G = MemoryHigh artifact proving the backstop works). Governor at 0.6G: floor((11604-2500)/1024/0.6)=14 -> seat_max=min(24,14)=14 (was 5 on 1.5G). 0.6 = measured p95 ~0.5G × 1.2 margin, floor 0.5. The governor is a PACING HINT; the 12G cap and per-worker 6G max are the actual safety layers. If pressure exceeds ~10% sustained or oomd kills become routine, raise toward 1.0-1.5. Re-derive with bin/ram-measure + bin/ram-metric-compare. HISTORY: #489 1.5 = min(memory.current p95 * 3, 1.5); earlier 0.75 was median completed-unit MemoryPeak (n=14, p95 4.4G, max 4.8G) pre-per-worker-caps. Per-task-weight cap: NOT applied.
